title: OAuth Server Settings
description: Configure the OAuth 2.1 authorization server. Used by AI clients (Claude, Cursor) via dynamic registration and by third-party integrations (ActivePieces, Zapier) via admin-created static clients. Run tcms oauth:setup once to generate the RSA signing key pair before enabling.

enabled.label: Enable OAuth Server
enabled.help: Master switch for the OAuth 2.1 authorization server. When off, the OAuth discovery documents and endpoints return 404, so MCP clients that see a discoverable OAuth server (Claude, Claude Desktop) connect anonymously to the public tier instead of demanding a login. Turn off to run a public-only MCP site — access is then anonymous (public collections) or API key (admin). Existing access tokens expire naturally (default 1 hour) and cannot be refreshed.

dynamicRegistration.label: Allow Dynamic Registration
dynamicRegistration.help: Enable RFC 7591 self-registration at POST /oauth/register. Off by default — it's an unauthenticated endpoint that writes server state. MCP clients (Claude Desktop, Cursor) need this on to connect without manual setup. Left off, create admin static clients for each integration. Self-registration alone never grants data access (a registered client still needs admin consent), but an open endpoint invites client-record flooding and consent-phishing.

accessTokenTtl.label: Access Token Lifetime
accessTokenTtl.help: How long an access token is valid. PHP DateInterval spec — e.g. PT1H (1 hour), PT15M (15 minutes), P1D (1 day). Shorter = better security (revocation more effective) but more refresh round-trips. Default 1h is the OAuth common middle ground.

refreshTokenTtl.label: Refresh Token Lifetime
refreshTokenTtl.help: How long a refresh token can be used to obtain new access tokens. After this, the user must re-authorize via the consent screen. Common values: P30D (30 days), P90D (90 days), P1Y (1 year). Default 30 days.

authCodeTtl.label: Authorization Code Lifetime
authCodeTtl.help: How long an authorization code is valid before it must be exchanged for tokens. Short by design — the user is mid-flow. RFC 6749 §4.1.2 recommends 10 minutes maximum. PT10M default.

tokenEndpointLimit.label: Token Endpoint Rate Limit (per minute)
tokenEndpointLimit.help: Maximum requests to /oauth/token per minute from a single IP. Protects against brute-force code exchange and runaway refresh loops. Applies to all callers (admin requests are NOT exempt). Set to 0 to disable. Default 60.

dynamicRegistrationLimit.label: Dynamic Registration Rate Limit (per hour)
dynamicRegistrationLimit.help: Maximum requests to /oauth/register per hour from a single IP. Dynamic registration is the abuse vector for client-record flooding — an unauthenticated endpoint that creates persistent server state. Default 10/hour by design. Set to 0 to disable.
